source.author: R. P. Bielat, D. E. Harrison and D. A. Coppolino

figure.title: Figure 16 (continued). (b) Drag coefficient. Aerodynamic characteristics of the body alone.
figure.x_axis: Drag coefficient, C_D, on staggered scales. Common axis = the M = 0.50 scale: left frame line = 0, grid every 0.002, right frame line = 0.060 (31 vertical lines, about 74 px apart). The label strip under the alpha = -2 line reads '0 for M = 0.50 .70 .85 .90 .925 .95 .975 1.00 1.02 1.035 1.085 1.10 1.13'; the row of '0' labels under the strip sits under every second grid line (left frame, then every 0.004), each '0' directly below its Mach number, followed by .004 .008 .012 on the M = 1.13 scale (.012 at the right frame).
figure.y_axis: Angle of attack, alpha, deg (common to all Mach numbers). Grid every 1 deg from -2 (the line above the label strip) to 14 (top frame line).
figure.content_note: Body alone. One faired polar per Mach number, 13 Mach numbers, hollow symbols with a centre dot, one shape per Mach number (identified by the M labels along the top of the plot, each above its polar). Only the symbols at nominal alpha = -2, 0 and +2 deg are read here. Every Mach number has two symbols at alpha = 0 (repeated test point), overlapping in all cases except M = 0.50; where the dot of one of them is hidden under or merged with the other's outline its centre is placed by eye (snap 'none', see notes).

calibration.x_definition: Common axis = the M = 0.50 C_D scale (its zero is the left frame line). Each Mach number's C_D = 0 is the grid line above its '0' label: M 0.50 at 0.000, 0.70 at 0.004, 0.85 at 0.008, 0.90 at 0.012, 0.925 at 0.016, 0.95 at 0.020, 0.975 at 0.024, 1.00 at 0.028, 1.02 at 0.032, 1.035 at 0.036, 1.085 at 0.040, 1.10 at 0.044, 1.13 at 0.048 (then .004, .008, .012 of the M = 1.13 scale = 0.052, 0.056, 0.060, the right frame). Reported C_D = common-axis value minus x_offset.
